title: The phantom city (Kern ch. 7)
hookLine: a guide conjures a city so tired travelers can rest, then says the treasure is further on
tomorrow: The jewel in the coat (Kern ch. 8)

lines: A HUT PAST THE NEXT BEND.
cards: Halfway up a hard trail, the group has stopped talking. Legs are shaking. Someone says what everyone is thinking: let's just go back down.
And the trip leader says: there's a hut just past the next bend. They make it. They rest.
And later, rested, they find the summit was closer than they thought. Chapter seven of the Lotus ends with a guide like that, though his hut is something stranger.

teach.b: In Kern's translation the Buddha tells of a great crowd setting out across a wild and fearful forest, on a long road, to reach a place of treasure. Their guide is wise and knows every turn.
But partway along the travelers are worn out and frightened. We can't go on, they say; let's turn back. The guide doesn't scold them.
He is skilled in means, the sutra says, and he feels for them. So, by his own power, he makes a city appear in the middle of the wilderness. Look, he says, here is a city.
Go in and rest. The travelers are delighted. They go in, rest, feel safe, and think they have arrived.

teach.h: A CITY MADE TO REST IN.
teach.b: When the guide sees they are rested, he makes the city vanish, and tells them: that city was something I made for you to rest in. The treasure is near. Come, let's go on.
Then the Buddha explains. He is the guide, and the road is long and hard. If beings heard only about the far goal, Buddhahood, many would lose heart and turn back.
So he teaches a resting place along the way: the peace, the release, the disciples have reached. It is real rest, given out of care. But it is not the end.
The treasure, the Buddha's own awakening, is further on.
Look at what the city is not.
It isn't a trick to punish anyone, or a test. It's there because tired people need somewhere to sit down, and the guide stays with them the whole way.
Carts, a dirt heap, rain, and now shelter: rest is part of the road.

how: The parable of the conjured city, which closes chapter seven of the Lotus Sutra, is taught in East Asian Buddhism as a picture of skillful means: the rest of the disciples' release is real, offered out of compassion, and the road goes on to Buddhahood.

o: a resting place the guide conjures on the long road
a heaven where the good go to rest for all time
a city of ghosts that travelers are told to avoid

games.q: a city to rest in: tap the pairs.
p: a resting place along the way

s: the guide scolds the travelers for wanting to turn back
he feels for them, and makes a city where they can rest.
the guide makes the city vanish once the travelers are rested
then he tells them he made it for their rest, and the treasure is near.
in the parable the city is the travelers' final goal
it is a resting place; the treasure lies further on.

games.q: you are the guide. your travelers are exhausted and frightened, and they want to turn back. the treasure is still far. what do you do?
o: tell them the full distance so they know
make a city appear so they can rest
leave them and go on alone
games.why: he conjures a city in the wilderness; when they are rested, he makes it vanish and tells them the treasure is near.

practice: For the first part of the sit, rest completely: shoulders drop, jaw loosens, hands go heavy, nowhere to get to. Let this moment be the city in the wilderness.
Toward the end, bring to mind one thing waiting for you today, and turn toward it, rested, the way the travelers turned back to the road.

wordCard.voice: The phantom city. In chapter seven, a guide conjures a city so worn-out travelers can rest, then tells them the treasure lies further on. Today's word.

orig.note: Sanskrit: city, town; in chapter seven, a city the guide makes appear in the wilderness.

carryVoice: Your line: a city to rest in. A real rest, and then the road again. Go gently.
